analysis.scope_and_question: This review examines the relationship among Nipah virus (NiV) spillover, Pteropus medius bat microbiota, and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) within a One Health framework, focusing on zoonotic transmission pathways and environmental factors in Bangladesh.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar to identify relevant peer-reviewed studies published between 2006 and 2025.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Pteropus medius bats harbor clinically important resistant bacteria, including ESBL-producing Escherichia coli, Salmonella spp., and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus spp. Habitat fragmentation, wastewater contamination, urbanization, agricultural intensification, and increased human-wildlife interactions are major drivers facilitating both NiV spillover and AMR dissemination.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies bidirectional exchange of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) among wildlife, livestock, and humans in bat roosts near agricultural lands, wastewater discharge sites, and peri-urban settlements, though specific mechanisms and quantitative data remain limited.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Integrated One Health surveillance and environmental management strategies are recommended to mitigate future zoonotic and AMR threats in Bangladesh, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions in high-risk interfaces.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review examines the interconnected risks of Nipah virus spillover and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) from Pteropus medius bats within a One Health framework. The study identifies bats as reservoirs for both NiV and clinically important resistant bacteria, with habitat fragmentation, wastewater contamination, and urbanization driving both spillover and AMR dissemination. Evidence suggests bidirectional exchange of resistance genes among wildlife, livestock, and humans in peri-urban interfaces. The review underscores the importance of integrated surveillance and environmental management to mitigate these dual threats in Bangladesh.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Nipah virus (NiV) infection causes fatal acute respiratory and neurological disease, and survivors may develop long-term sequelae or experience relapsing encephalitis months to years after recovery. The basis of divergent disease trajectories and incomplete viral clearance remains poorly defined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We established a red-shifted bioluminescent resonance energy transfer reporter system to enable longitudinal tracking of NiV infection in vivo and applied it in mouse models of infection.
analysis.methods: We integrated longitudinal in vivo imaging with RT-qPCR, histopathology, and in situ hybridization to study NiV infection in IFNAR-/- mice, examining route-, strain-, and immune-dependent differences in viral dissemination and clearance.
analysis.main_results: Intranasal infection remained largely confined to the respiratory tract, while intraperitoneal infection resulted in systemic spread followed by prolonged, fluctuating focal viral signal detectable up to 42 days post-infection. Persistent viral RNA was detected in discrete brain regions after apparent clinical recovery, indicating anatomically restricted persistence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal the spatiotemporal dynamics of incomplete NiV clearance in vivo and provide a framework to study relapsing disease, demonstrating asynchronous and focal CNS involvement.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results improve understanding of NiV persistence and relapsing encephalitis, informing surveillance strategies and therapeutic approaches targeting anatomically restricted viral reservoirs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in IFNAR-/- mice, which may not fully recapitulate human immune responses; however, the longitudinal imaging approach provides high-confidence evidence of viral dynamics.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated Nipah virus (NiV) clearance dynamics using longitudinal in vivo imaging in IFNAR-/- mice. The researchers developed a bioluminescent reporter system to track infection over time, revealing that intraperitoneal infection leads to systemic spread and prolonged focal viral signal in the CNS, detectable up to 42 days post-infection. Despite apparent clinical recovery, persistent viral RNA was found in discrete brain regions, indicating anatomically restricted persistence. The findings demonstrate asynchronous and incomplete viral clearance, providing insights into the mechanisms of relapsing encephalitis in survivors. This research offers a framework for studying relapsing disease and informs strategies for surveillance and targeted therapies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Nipah virus (NiV), a World Health Organization priority pathogen, is a lethal enveloped RNA virus within the Paramyxoviridae family. Despite past studies, several aspects of the molecular-level orchestration underlying this process, such as how F, G, and their interactions regulate fusion, remain poorly understood, obscured by challenges in decoupling fusion determinants in complex cellular environments.
analysis.study_design_and_population: NiV attachment G and fusion F glycoproteins execute viral-cell or cell-cell membrane fusion during viral entry and syncytia formation, respectively. Here, we report a reconstitution-based approach for mimicking the NiV-host interface, employing virus-like particles with NiV M, F, and/or G proteins and plasma membrane vesicles derived from NiV-permissive host cells.
analysis.methods: We found this minimal system can accurately recapitulate NiV-host cell fusion, and used this platform for biophysical dissection of NiV fusion using wild-type or mutant F and G proteins affecting fusion at distinct intermediate steps.
analysis.main_results: We show that F and G affect hemifusion and pore formation stages of NiV fusion in distinct ways, revealing a tightly regulated fusion landscape.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Our approach also delivers one of the first direct measurements of temperature thresholds for NiV fusion, providing novel insights into energetic requirements underlying viral fusogenicity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings demonstrate the power of this approach in dissecting aspects of NiV fusion not accessible via cell-based assays. Thus, this study serves as a blueprint for comprehensive fusion analysis of other viruses with multicomponent fusion machinery and host protein receptors, and could be repurposed into therapeutic screening platforms targeting their fusion mechanisms, necessary for developing novel antivirals.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength for the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the molecular mechanisms of Nipah virus (NiV) entry by examining the roles of its attachment (G) and fusion (F) glycoproteins. The research highlights the challenges in understanding how these proteins regulate fusion in complex cellular environments. A reconstitution-based approach was developed to mimic the NiV-host interface using virus-like particles and plasma membrane vesicles. The results show that F and G proteins influence different stages of the fusion process, revealing a tightly regulated mechanism. The study provides novel insights into the temperature thresholds required for NiV fusion, offering a biophysical framework for analyzing viral fusogenicity. These findings could inform the development of antiviral therapies targeting NiV's fusion process. The study's results are based on a minimal system that accurately recapitulates NiV-host cell fusion, but the evidence does not explicitly address limitations or the strength of the findings.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Nipah virus (NiV) poses a major risk to global public health due to its high infectivity and associated mortality rates, and currently no licensed vaccines or antiviral medications are available for NiV infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study employed computational methods to design a peptide-ligand conjugate (PLC) immunotherapeutic approach targeting NiV-infected cells, leveraging pre-existing immune responses in NiV-endemic populations.
analysis.methods: We employed biomolecular modeling (in silico) to establish binding affinities and perform docking studies using a compound library from the MolProphet database, with a non-cleavable oxime linker selected for enhanced stability and conjugation.
analysis.main_results: The PLC design demonstrated selective binding capacity to a transmembrane protein present on NiV-infected cells, with the oxime linker providing enhanced stability and the peptide epitope design incorporating regions associated with established long-term immunity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This PLC system represents a promising framework for antiviral therapeutic development by harnessing pre-existing immune recognition to promote selective clearance of NiV-infected cells, highlighting critical structural components and functional roles of PLCs in therapeutic development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into drug target screening and rational design strategies for enhancing targeting specificity and molecular stability of immunotherapeutics against NiV infection, with future work needed for experimental validation and efficacy studies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate as the study relies solely on computational modeling without experimental validation, limiting confidence in the actual therapeutic efficacy of the proposed PLC design.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the urgent need for Nipah virus (NiV) therapeutics by computationally designing a peptide-ligand conjugate (PLC) immunotherapeutic approach. The PLC selectively targets NiV-infected cells by exploiting pre-existing immune responses in endemic populations, using a non-cleavable oxime linker for stability and immunogenic epitopes from measles, mumps, and rubella vaccines. Computational modeling confirmed selective binding to a transmembrane protein on infected cells and enhanced stability. While the findings offer a promising framework for antiviral development, the evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of experimental validation. Future work should focus on in vitro and in vivo efficacy studies to confirm the therapeutic potential of this approach.

060c35b9dba4828ad0f4741c619d96cf4da5fa3b.text: 来自中狐蝠的健康见解:尼帕病毒 跨物种溢出、微生物群和抗菌素耐药性。

fd619150b5cb90f52855c26f41ceeb5025465096.text: 中翼龙是 尼帕病毒 (NiV) 的主要 储存宿主,尼帕病毒 (NiV) 是一种人畜共患病原体,导致孟加拉国反复出现致命的 脑炎 暴发。人类感染主要与食用被蝙蝠排泄物污染的生枣椰汁有关。除了病毒 跨物种溢出 之外,越来越多的证据表明,与蝙蝠相关的微生物群和鸟粪是抗菌素耐药性 (AMR) 的潜在 储存宿主,有助于耐药细菌和耐药基因的环境传播。这篇叙述性文献综述研究了 One Health 框架内 NiV 跨物种溢出、蝙蝠微生物群和 AMR 之间的关系。使用 PubMed、Scopus、Web of Science、ScienceDirect 和 Google Scholar 进行结构化文献检索,以识别 2006 年至 2025 年间发表的相关同行评审研究。审查的证据表明,翼龙种群含有临床上重要的耐药细菌,包括产生 ESBL(扩展谱β-内酰胺酶)的大肠杆菌、沙门氏菌和耐甲氧西林细菌。葡萄球菌属此外,最近的研究表明,农田、废水排放点和城郊居民点附近的蝙蝠栖息地可能促进野生动物、牲畜和人类之间 ARG 的双向交换。栖息地破碎化、废水污染、城市化、农业集约化以及人类与野生动物相互作用的增加被认为是促进 NiV 跨物种溢出 和抗菌素耐药性传播的主要驱动因素。总体而言,文献证明了人为环境干扰、人畜共患病 跨物种溢出 风险以及蝙蝠相关系统中抗生素耐药性的出现之间存在显着的生态关联。这些发现凸显了综合 One Health 监测 和环境管理战略对于减轻孟加拉国未来人畜共患病和抗菌素耐药性威胁的重要性。

b1acfa98ee19872c6d266f6f83ac09b74eebcebb.text: 本综述探讨了 One Health 框架内 尼帕病毒 (NiV) 跨物种溢出、Pteropus medius 蝙蝠微生物群和抗菌素耐药性 (AMR) 之间的关系,重点关注孟加拉国的人畜共患 传播 途径和环境因素。

9850d20bc204ba217867a48312b82fac7320a8e0.text: 使用 PubMed、Scopus、Web of Science、ScienceDirect 和 Google Scholar 进行叙述性文献综述,以确定 2006 年至 2025 年间发表的相关同行评审研究。

2378bee9851c593e87816d7123dde9ea7a332932.text: Pteropus medius 蝙蝠体内含有临床上重要的耐药细菌,包括产 ESBL 的大肠杆菌、沙门氏菌和耐甲氧西林葡萄球菌。栖息地破碎化、废水污染、城市化、农业集约化以及人类与野生动物相互作用的增加是促进 NiV 跨物种溢出 和抗菌素耐药性传播的主要驱动因素。

c546b9e9c357d6b2922519d5654dad84953100ee.text: 尽管具体机制和定量数据仍然有限,但该综述确定了农田、废水排放点和城郊住区附近的蝙蝠栖息地的野生动物、牲畜和人类之间存在抗菌素耐药基因(ARG)的双向交换。

2705c3c516049cc9abe40fafa13f2c5052e53e71.text: 建议采用综合 One Health 监测 和环境管理策略来减轻孟加拉国未来的人畜共患病和抗菌素耐药性威胁,强调需要对高风险界面进行有针对性的干预措施。

96cc28be886aa3f5822efed933bc3ea297daa871.text: 纵向体内成像揭示了 IFNAR-/- 小鼠中异步、不完全的 尼帕病毒 清除与长期局灶性 CNS 受累。

8d3570c4ef1fdfd4ce8c9f92248aa60fab55d59c.text: 尼帕病毒 (NiV) 感染会导致致命的急性呼吸道和神经系统疾病。幸存者可能会出现长期后遗症或在康复后数月至数年经历复发 脑炎。不同的疾病轨迹和不完全的病毒清除的基础仍然不明确。在这里,我们建立了红移生物发光共振能量转移报告系统,以实现体内 NiV 感染的纵向追踪,并将其应用于小鼠感染模型。我们证明了 NiV 感染后传播的途径、毒株和免疫依赖性差异,并揭示了空间异质和异步的病毒清除。虽然鼻内感染仍然主要局限于呼吸道,但腹膜内感染会导致全身性传播,随后在 IFNAR -/- 小鼠中感染后长达 42 天可检测到长期、波动的局灶性病毒信号。与 RT-qPCR、组织病理学和原位杂交的整合显示,在明显的临床恢复后,离散的大脑区域中存在持续的病毒 RNA,表明解剖学上限制的持续性。总之,这些发现揭示了体内不完全 NiV 清除的时空动态,并为研究复发性疾病提供了框架。

b367a43d79f37f3509472a36f033ae2223ddf129.text: 这些结果提高了对 NiV 持续性和复发性 脑炎 的理解,为针对解剖学限制性病毒 储存宿主 的 监测 策略和治疗方法提供了信息。

7ceec3dbd36d1e7dbe3181ac8c58e92756d71f7d.text: 该研究是在 IFNAR-/- 小鼠中进行的,可能无法完全重现人类 免疫应答;然而,纵向成像方法提供了病毒动力学的高可信度证据。

0231fd41c61c23afee6361f3ebe11da59c38656c.text: 尼帕病毒 附着和融合糖蛋白在进入过程中发挥的独特作用的生物物理学阐明。

e6373222f81aa0af0bac67602e1415556bd3c4f5.text: 尼帕病毒 (NiV) 是世界卫生组织优先病原体,是副粘病毒科中的一种致命的有包膜 RNA 病毒。NiV附着G和融合F糖蛋白分别在病毒进入和合胞体形成过程中执行病毒-细胞或细胞-细胞膜融合。尽管有过去的研究,但这一过程背后的分子水平编排的几个方面,例如 F、G 及其相互作用如何调节融合,仍然知之甚少,并被复杂细胞环境中解耦融合决定因素的挑战所掩盖。在这里,我们报告了一种基于重构的方法,用于模拟 NiV-宿主 界面,采用带有 NiV M、F 和/或 G 蛋白的病毒样颗粒以及源自 NiV 允许的 宿主 细胞的质膜囊泡。我们发现这个最小的系统可以准确地重现 NiV-宿主 细胞融合,并使用该平台使用野生型或突变型 F 和 G 蛋白在不同的中间步骤影响融合,对 NiV 融合进行生物物理解剖。我们发现 F 和 G 以不同的方式影响 NiV 融合的半融合和孔隙形成阶段,揭示了严格调控的融合景观。我们的方法还提供了第一个直接测量 NiV 融合温度阈值的方法,为病毒融合性的能量需求提供了新的见解。这些发现证明了这种方法在剖析 NiV 融合方面的能力,这是通过基于细胞的测定无法实现的。因此,这项研究可以作为具有多组分融合机制和 宿主 蛋白受体的其他病毒的综合融合分析的蓝图,并且可以重新用于针对其融合机制的治疗筛选平台,这对于开发新型 抗病毒药物 是必需的。

53f9517842eb00e37c06002602a7481639d6c469.text: 用于 尼帕病毒 感染靶向治疗的免疫原性肽-配体缀合物的计算设计

81c83e0ce7aa1b8b6e5524a9342d1ca7958e3d3c.text: 简介 尼帕病毒 (NiV) 由于其高传染性和相关的 死亡率 率,对全球公共卫生构成重大风险。目前,尚无获得许可的 疫苗 或 抗病毒药物 药物可用于治疗 NiV 感染,因此临床管理仅限于支持性护理。负责将 NiV 与 宿主 细胞受体 (ephrin-B2/B3) 结合的病毒受体糖蛋白代表了理想的治疗靶点。这项研究提出了一种新型肽-配体缀合物 (PLC) 免疫治疗方法,该方法利用 NiV 流行人群中预先存在的 免疫应答 来选择性地靶向和消除受感染的细胞。方法我们采用生物分子建模(计算机)来建立结合亲和力,并使用从 MolProphet 数据库获得的化合物库进行对接研究。选择不可裂解的肟接头来增强物理稳定性并确保配体和肽组分之间的牢固结合。该肽经过工程改造,含有源自麻疹、腮腺炎和风疹 疫苗 的免疫原性最小表位区域,这些区域是根据居住在 NiV 流行地区的个体的高免疫率和长效记忆反应而选择的。结果 PLC 设计证明了对 NiV 感染细胞上存在的跨膜蛋白的选择性结合能力。肟接头提供了增强的稳定性,肽表位设计成功地整合了与已建立的长期免疫相关的区域。讨论 该 PLC 系统通过利用预先存在的免疫识别来促进 NiV 感染细胞的选择性清除,为 抗病毒药物 治疗开发提供了一个有前途的框架。研究结果强调了 PLC 在治疗开发中的关键结构成分和功能作用,包括药物靶点筛选和增强靶向特异性和分子稳定性的合理设计策略。未来的工作应侧重于计算预测的实验验证和体外/体内功效研究。

d7c477d16466165594ffb6c20d3570941ff1458b.text: 尼帕病毒 (NiV) 由于其高传染性和相关的 死亡率 发病率,对全球公共卫生构成重大风险,目前尚无获得许可的 疫苗 或 抗病毒药物 药物可用于治疗 NiV 感染。

6364a15e972ca73090a9875d8abc43bffda7902d.text: 这些研究结果为药物靶点筛选和合理设计策略提供了见解,以增强针对 NiV 感染的免疫疗法的靶向特异性和分子稳定性,未来还需要开展实验验证和疗效研究。
